verifier_note: Every one of the 14 citations resolves and none is fabricated; I reached the primary licence surface for all 14, including two PDFs, four Google-Sites/lab pages and six API records. Ten findings needed correction, but only three move a bottom line: NUS-48E does carry a research-only agreement inside its Drive README, OpenSinger's '2.0' pin is contradicted by a CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 LICENSE file in the same repo, and California AB 1836 took effect 1 Jan 2025 rather than 2026. The systemic problem this lane keeps surfacing is real and reproduced repeatedly: the licence a paper states and the licence its download surface declares are different artifacts (GTSinger, OpenSinger, Opencpop's own meta tag, NHSS's two EULAs).

verdicts.verify_note: Zenodo record 1193957 declares SPDX id cc-by-4.0; DataCite rightsList reads 'Creative Commons Attribution 4.0'. ISMIR paper: 10.1h, 20 singers (11M/9F), 17 techniques, labels only in folder/filenames. Zenodo answered today; 504 caveat moot.

Absence holds for the lab page, Drive link surface and paper - but README.txt inside the corpus folder reads 'shared with the agreement that it will be used solely for research purposes'. Research-only is sourced, not inferred.

corrections.claim: The 'no licence anywhere' headline is wrong. Verified absent from the SMC-NUS lab page (zero hits on licen/terms/agreement/copyright in the raw HTML), from the paper, and from the Drive folder listing - but README.txt inside the nus-smc-corpus_48 folder states the dataset 'is being shared with the agreement that it will be used solely for research purposes', plus a citation requirement. A research-only use restriction therefore does exist in the distribution, and Shi et al.'s 'Research-only' classification is traceable to it rather than being the survey authors' inference. Every number checks out (48 recordings / 20 unique songs, 12 subjects, 169 min total, 115 min = 1.9 h sung, 25,474 phone instances). Bottom line COMMERCIAL USE: NO is unchanged and now affirmatively grounded.

verdicts.verify_note: Art.30-4 reliance, zunko.jp letter of intent and label-only GitHub all verified verbatim. But a licensor grant does exist: the zunko agreement licenses non-commercially and gates shipping a trained model. Ogawa is Univ. of Yamanashi.

corrections.authors: Ogawa, Itsuki (University of Yamanashi); Morise, Masanori (Meiji University); singer Himika Akaneya
corrections.claim: The framing 'there is no licence because there is no licensor grant; the corpus rides a statutory exception' is wrong. zunko.jp/kiridev/login.php (HTTP 200) carries an 8-article agreement between the user, SSS LLC and Meiji University/Morise whose Article 1 expressly licenses the data non-commercially. The contract goes well beyond certifying Art. 30-4 purpose: mandatory (C)SSS credit, no redistribution, no commercial use of outputs, PRIOR SSS APPROVAL before embedding a trained model in any released software or service, destroy-on-termination, Tokyo District Court jurisdiction. So downstream work inherits a contractual model-release gate, not merely a jurisdiction-bound statutory exception - the conclusion COMMERCIAL USE: NO is reinforced, but for contract reasons as much as statutory ones. Minor: singing duration is ~57 min; the paper is AST vol 42 issue 3, pp.140-145.

verdicts.verify_note: ACE licence cc-by-nc-4.0 confirmed at the HF card; the authors' legal/ethical caution is verbatim; SingNet confirmed in full and its project page is still 404 today. Fixes: the kising HF id is wrong (401), and the ACE paper is 2024.

corrections.claim: Two fixes. (1) espnet/kising-v2-segments returns HTTP 401 at both the API and the page; the live repo is espnet/ace-kising-segments, also cardData.license cc-by-nc-4.0. The paper's own footnote still cites the stale name, so the finding faithfully copied a renamed artifact - but the id as written does not resolve. It is also a dataset paper with a comparison table, not a survey. Everything else verified: 128.9h/30 vocalists and 32.5h/34 vocalists from Table 1, ACE Studio 1.7.2 synthesis with manual F0/breath/vibrato/duration tuning, the caution sentence verbatim, SingNet's 3,000h / 2,629+321 split / MDX23 / streaming-platform sourcing, and zero licence, copyright, ethics or consent text anywhere in the SingNet paper.

S.4591 exact: intro 2026-05-20, reported 2026-06-18 unanimous, Senate Legislative Calendar 2026-06-24; nonprofit library/archive/educational exemption verbatim; ELVIS Act exact. But AB 1836 took effect 1 Jan 2025, not 2026.

corrections.claim: California AB 1836 took effect 1 JANUARY 2025, not 1 January 2026. It was chaptered 17 Sept 2024 as Ch. 258, Stats. 2024, contains no urgency clause and no delayed operative date, so Cal. Const. art. IV s8(c) puts it in force 1 Jan 2025; two independent practitioner sources state the same. AB 2602 (Ch. 259) likewise applies to performances fixed on or after 1 Jan 2025. The signing date of 17 September 2024 is correct for both. Everything else verified at source: the AI & SOCIETY paper (Cotton, Holzapfel, de Vries, Berglund, Tatar; 12 July 2026; CC BY 4.0; EASE applied to three singing datasets); the ELVIS Act (effective 1 July 2024, voice as property right covering actual and simulated voice, liability for distributing technology whose 'primary purpose or function' is producing a particular identifiable individual's voice, knowledge standard, label standing, civil plus Class A misdemeanour); and S.4591's full procedural history, licensable property right, notice-and-takedown regime, news/commentary/criticism/parody carve-outs and the nonprofit-only research exemption.

verdicts.verify_note: The 2.0 pin does not hold. Release page names no licence; repo README's visible text is unversioned 'CC BY-NC-SA' with only the href at 2.0, and the LICENSE file beside it is 'Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International'.

corrections.claim: Not 'CC BY-NC-SA 2.0 as stated on the release page'. multi-singer.github.io names no licence at all (only 'the dataset sharing license', unnamed). The repo README links CC BY-NC-SA to the 2.0 legalcode URL but its visible text carries no version, and the repo's own LICENSE file is the full CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 text (3x '4.0 International', zero mentions of 2.0). GitHub's detector returns NOASSERTION. The version is unresolved, not pinned at 2.0. Access is also no longer by application - that gate was deleted 2022-11-19; the page now links the tarball directly. Commercial use remains NO on either version. '1,146 songs' is not in the paper (secondary survey tables only), and the 93-vs-66 singer gap is an inconsistency inside one paragraph of the paper, not a paper-vs-release-page gap.

corrections.claim: Two different EULAs are live and the finding describes the unlinked one. NUSLicence.pdf, titled 'NHSS Database END USER LICENSE AGREEMENT (04/2020)', has 14 sections and is not linked from index.html or download.html. The operative surface embedded in download.html is NUSLicence-GLC-Bidisha.pdf, a 2021 NUS legal revision with 15 sections; it retains s.1 'This License is an Open Source License', s.4 internal/non-commercial/research-only, s.5 sign-and-email, s.6 'Copyleft and Open Science', s.7 redistribution ban, s.8 audio-visual scope and s.9 commercial ban, but DELETES the s.10 'Small portions ... cannot be used in any publication' clause and adds a s.13 termination clause. Also: sung duration is 4.75 h; download.html directs the signed PDF to a gmail contact address as well as haizhou.li@nus.edu.sg; and the 'copy-paste from an unrelated audio-visual EULA' origin is a reasonable inference (the sentence describes AV16.3) but no source EULA carrying it was retrievable, so it is unproven.
